localBiteReport: The week of September 4–10, 2026 brought the first clear signs of the fall transition to Choctawhatchee Bay, according to Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters (Destin area). Large schools of baitfish — greenies and pogies — have been pushing from open deeper water into the bayous, flats, and bridge areas, which is starting to wake up the inshore bite. Redfish action on the flats is improving and is expected to build significantly through the rest of September as the mullet migration gets underway; Blake anticipates the first strong slot-redfish bite arriving in the second or third week of the month. Speckled trout have been holding around grass, sandy pockets, docks, and deeper cuts throughout the bay, and bull reds have been showing around Rocky Bayou, Boggy Bayou, Joe's Bayou, Marler Bayou, and the East Pass — responding to topwater plugs and large swimbaits worked through feeding baitfish schools. Water temperature at this location is 87°F, which is keeping midday fishing slow; early morning remains the most productive window for inshore species.
